concepts.title: Agent harness
concepts.definition: The context, permission and environment Concorde gives one agent, applied through the agent program's own configuration: a worker's by the worker harness from its grant, a task session's by Coordination from its task, the main agent's by its installed guidance alone.

concepts.title: Boundary
concepts.definition: The read and write limits one worker's job receives, fixed by its task type and its bound Modules.

contrasts.reason: a worker's boundary comes from its task type's grant; a task session has no task type and receives only the session boundary, which keeps its writes inside its task

concepts.title: Boundary case
concepts.definition: One of the four explanations of a refused read, write or tool: overreaching work, a wrong project Spec, a Concorde implementation bug or a Concorde design limitation.

concepts.title: Boundary set
concepts.definition: One of the seven sets the Protocol derives for a Module: its Spec context, external context, implementation context, Spec scope or implementation scope, or the project-wide ProjectImplementation or ProjectSpecification shared by every Module.

concepts.title: Brief
concepts.definition: The prompt a worker receives: its caller's task instructions followed by the grant's `rw`, `ro` and `names` lists as absolute paths and the rules of its boundary.

concepts.title: Brownfield workflow
concepts.definition: The workflow that describes a project whose code came before its Specs: survey, scaffold, code_to_spec per Module, spec review, task validation and delivery.

concepts.title: Build manifest
concepts.definition: The generated record of the digest of every source the build read and of every output it wrote.

concepts.title: Capability context
concepts.definition: The tools a worker may use, the contracts those tools reach and the contract of the worker result it must end with, which tell it what it can do and never what the project promises.

concepts.title: Check result
concepts.definition: The record of one configured check run: the check, its Module, the status, the exit code, the digest of what was measured and the saved log with its digest.

concepts.title: Concorde defect
concepts.definition: A failure, wrong behaviour or design limitation of Concorde that would happen in any project using Concorde the same way, as opposed to a problem of the project it was seen in.

concepts.title: Concorde repository
concepts.definition: The independent Git repository of Concorde that a develop install is made and updated from, and in which the Concorde defects it reports are fixed.

concepts.title: Configured check
concepts.definition: A command that a Module's own checks file, `.concorde/checks/<module id>.json`, assigns to that Module, with its arguments, time limit and the input paths its result depends on.

concepts.title: Context
concepts.definition: Everything one worker may know: the union of its Spec context, external context, implementation context, capability context and task context.

concepts.title: Context identity
concepts.definition: The digest of the selected Spec sources and pinned external material together with the declarations that selected them, and, for a task type that reads every Module's Specs, of all of them.

concepts.title: Decision log
concepts.definition: The Markdown file `decisions.md` in a task's folder in which the session working on the task writes the choices it made without the developer, and to which escalations, the task sessions' reports and the main agent's answers are appended; when the task ends it is committed to the primary branch as `.concorde/decisions/<history key>.md`.

concepts.title: Decision point
concepts.definition: An item a run's output lists, under the workflow step output convention, as to be settled above the task before an interactive workflow goes on, by the main agent when its authority covers it and otherwise by the developer; the Operation that produces it decides which of its decisions and open questions are such points.

concepts.title: Decomposition proposal
concepts.definition: The output of a survey: the child Modules to create with their purposes, bound entries and uses, the checks it proposes, the decisions it took and its open questions.

concepts.title: Defect report
concepts.definition: An Issue report the project's main agent writes about a Concorde defect, naming the project and Concorde commit it was seen on and carrying the whole error chain.

concepts.title: Delivery commit
concepts.definition: A commit on the first-parent history of a workspace's branch, since its base commit, whose subject is exactly `concorde: deliver <workspace>`, which marks the workspace delivered when it verifies by having exactly one parent; delivering commands such as Method's `delivery` and Coordination's `task deliver` make it.

concepts.title: Deny rules
concepts.definition: The `permissions.deny` entries of the worker settings that forbid the file tools every path the grant does not make readable or writable.

concepts.title: Detached run
concepts.definition: A run whose runner the command starts as a process of its own, printing the run identity at once instead of waiting for the result.

concepts.title: Develop install
concepts.definition: An installation of Concorde into a project from the clean primary worktree of a Concorde repository the developer also changes, recorded as mode `develop` in the receipt and carrying Dogfooding's guidance.

concepts.title: Dogfood scenario
concepts.definition: A file naming a project, a fault, the developer's prompt and the expected outcome, under `scripts/e2e/scenarios/`.

concepts.title: Error chain
concepts.definition: The structured report of an error that travels up: one link per level that could not handle it, each with its detailed account and its reason for not handling it, and the errors it received from below nested as its causes.

concepts.title: Evidence
concepts.definition: A recorded check or review result, bound to the exact inputs it examined.

concepts.title: Execution command
concepts.definition: A deterministic `concorde` command, such as `task-validation`, `delivery` or `scaffold`, that launches no worker and is run and recorded by the Execution runner exactly like an Operation.

concepts.title: Execution runner
concepts.definition: The deterministic process that runs one Operation's or execution command's steps in its workspace, launches workers only through the steps that ask for them and writes the run result.

concepts.title: External context
concepts.definition: The pinned documentation and source of external dependencies that the bound Modules' `external` inclusions select: the Protocol's ExternalContext of those Modules, read only.

concepts.title: File transaction
concepts.definition: A set of whole-file writes, each bound to the digest of the bytes it replaces, whose failure observed by its process restores every file it wrote, a refused restoration being reported file by file.

concepts.title: Grant
concepts.definition: The per-path access list, each path at level `names`, `ro` or `rw`, that one task type assigns to the bound Modules, computed from one worktree's Specs and identified by its context identity.

concepts.title: Headless session
concepts.definition: A `claude -p` main session in a test project, run by the tool in one or more rounds and kept in a session directory.

concepts.title: History
concepts.definition: The folder `.concorde/history/` to which closing a task moves the task's whole folder, record, decision log and trace, where it is never changed, apart from the merge that closed the task finishing its answer, and retention only removes its conversation records or the whole folder.

contrasts.reason: the task record is the current state the task commands act on; the history keeps a closed task as it was

concepts.title: Impact index
concepts.definition: A derived reverse lookup that tells which Modules a change to a document, node, contract or file concerns.

concepts.title: Implementation context
concepts.definition: The code side of a worker's context: the names of the bound Modules' implementation files and, when the task type grants it, the whole project's code, the Protocol's ProjectImplementation, whose contents a task that reads code sees and whose names alone a review-architecture task sees.

concepts.title: Issue
concepts.definition: A durable, project-wide record of one concrete problem, kept by the primary worktree, holding every report made about it, each with its tier, and its disposition history.

concepts.title: Issue report
concepts.definition: One immutable observation inside an Issue: what was seen, why it matters, the basis for the claim, evidence locations and who reported it.

concepts.title: Issue revision
concepts.definition: The digest of an Issue record's exact bytes, used to refuse a write over a record that changed after it was read.

concepts.title: Issue severity
concepts.definition: How much the problem of an Issue report matters while it stands, independently of its tier: `critical`, `high`, `medium` or `low`, most severe first.

contrasts.reason: the tier says who may handle the problem; the severity says how much it matters, and so which Issues are fixed first

concepts.title: Issue tier
concepts.definition: The class an Issue report gives its problem by who may handle it without the level above: `suggestion`, which is advisory, or the blocking `obvious-fix`, `preferred-fix` and `decision-needed`.

concepts.title: Main agent
concepts.definition: The developer-facing Claude Code session, started in the primary worktree, that discusses the project, splits work into tasks, hands every task to a task session and answers it, and merges the delivered tasks, asking the developer every question a task needs.

concepts.title: Main-session guidance
concepts.definition: The instructions, installed as a project skill for Claude Code and as a block of the project's `CLAUDE.md`, that tell the main agent how to work with Concorde: Coordination's working method followed by the guidance each other installed part contributes.

concepts.title: Merge lock
concepts.definition: The lock `.concorde/locks/merge.lock` of the primary worktree that one process at a time holds while it changes the primary branch on Concorde's behalf, such as a task merge, open or close or an Issue write; the operating system releases it when that process ends.

concepts.title: Model map
concepts.definition: The user's JSON file outside every repository, `~/.config/concorde/models.json` unless `CONCORDE_MODEL_MAP` or `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` places it elsewhere, that gives each project model name of the worker configuration its local model id on pi, on Claude Code or both, and without whose entry for its backend a worker is refused.

contrasts.reason: the worker configuration is tracked and says which model each worker uses; the model map belongs to one machine and says how that machine's programs reach it

concepts.title: Module
concepts.definition: One cohesive responsibility of the software, with its own Spec; it need not be a package or directory.

concepts.title: Open question
concepts.definition: A behaviour the worker read but could not tell to be intended, reported with what it observed, why it is uncertain and the options, and written into no promise.

concepts.title: Operation
concepts.definition: A named job whose steps launch one or more AI workers, together with host steps and service calls, started with `concorde run` in a workspace, and that returns exactly one run result; the part that provides it registers its definition.

concepts.title: Operation catalog
concepts.definition: The list of Operations the installed parts register, giving for each its providing Module, its task type, the ids of its workers, whether it may run unbound, whether it may change the workspace and the contract of its output.

concepts.title: Optional integration
concepts.definition: A feature of one part that uses a part it does not depend on, which works when that part is installed and otherwise is skipped with a plain statement of what is missing, never failing for its absence.

concepts.title: Part
concepts.definition: One independently installable piece of Concorde, made of one top-level Module of the Framework with its children, that names the parts it depends on, works without every part it does not depend on and reaches any other only through an optional integration.

concepts.title: Part registration
concepts.definition: The plain data one installed part gives Distribution: its name, the parts it depends on, its commands, MCP tools, typed value types, guidance, install contributions and idle checks, from which the `concorde` command and the project MCP server are composed.

concepts.title: Permission extension
concepts.definition: The pi extension the Harness generates from a grant, which checks every file tool against it, runs every command in the sandbox and receives the worker result.

concepts.title: Progress file
concepts.definition: A worker run's `status.json` in its [run directory](#concept.run-directory), which the host keeps current while the worker runs so the main session can show what it is doing.

contrasts.reason: a worker run's progress file follows one worker; the run progress file follows the Operation or command run, which may launch several

concepts.title: Project MCP server
concepts.definition: The project's one stdio MCP server, `concorde project-mcp` registered as `concorde`, of which each Claude Code session runs its own process, that serves the MCP tools the installed parts register, answers each call with a fresh process of the Concorde the primary worktree's `concorde` runs at that moment, takes locks without waiting and hands a granted lock to the detached process doing the work, and wakes its session through a Claude Code channel when a registered wait is over.

contrasts.reason: the server never holds a lock it grants: the flock stays the only lock and belongs to the process doing the work

concepts.title: Protocol binding
concepts.definition: The project configuration's explicit acceptance of one installed Spec Protocol copy, recorded as its version and the digest of its manifest.

concepts.title: Protocol copy
concepts.definition: The rendered Spec Protocol bundle placed in a project under `.concorde/protocol/`, whose manifest digest the project configuration binds.

concepts.title: Read-only check boundary
concepts.definition: The Linux sandbox in which a check runs: the whole host filesystem read-only, one fresh writable scratch directory, private process and IPC namespaces, and the host's network.

concepts.title: Readiness
concepts.definition: The outcome of Validation's readiness steps in one `task-validation` or `delivery` run: whether the workspace may be delivered, with its blocking findings and the checks run, bound to a digest of the exact inputs examined.

concepts.title: Registry
concepts.definition: The project-wide index of Modules, which mirrors every Module's `module` block and is never itself a place where relations are declared.

concepts.title: Resume round
concepts.definition: One continuation of the same worker session with what its caller's round validation reports to repair, such as the failures of configured checks or the structural errors of what the worker wrote.

concepts.title: Review finding
concepts.definition: One problem a reviewer or architect establishes in the Specs of a reviewed Module, with its location, dimension, tier, evidence and a suggested repair, which the review reports as an Issue.

concepts.title: Review verdict
concepts.definition: The outcome of a Spec review or a Spec panel, derived by the Operation from the Issues that stand for each reviewed Module: `accepted`, `changes_required` or `incomplete`.

concepts.title: Run
concepts.definition: One execution of an Operation or an execution command in one worktree, with its own run identity, progress file and run result.

concepts.title: Run directory
concepts.definition: The [trace node](#concept.trace-node) `workers/<run-id>/` of one worker run, inside the node of the run that launched it, holding its run record, progress file, grant, brief, transcript and one node per round.

concepts.title: Run lock
concepts.definition: The file `locks/runs/<run-id>.lock` that a run's runner alone locks from before its first run progress file until after its result and removes as it exits, by which any observer tells, from any PID namespace, whether the run still runs.

contrasts.reason: the workspace lock keeps one workspace running one thing at a time; the run lock tells whether one run's runner still lives

concepts.title: Run progress file
concepts.definition: A run's `status.json` in its trace node, which the runner keeps current with what is running, where and in which step, and once finished with the status and summary.

concepts.title: Run record
concepts.definition: The host's durable record of one worker run, the `trace.json` of its [run directory](#concept.run-directory): its grant and context identity, settings, transcript, audits, round validations, rounds and result.

concepts.title: Run result
concepts.definition: The structured envelope every run returns and saves: what ran, in which workspace, its status, its output, the worker's claims when there was a worker, the runner's own evidence and, when it is not ok, its error chain.

concepts.title: Run store
concepts.definition: Where Execution keeps its runs as [trace nodes](#concept.trace-node): `runs/` of a workspace folder, the step nodes of its workflow, `.concorde/unbound/` of a worktree for unbound runs, and the lobby `.concorde/lobby/` for a bound run until it holds its workspace's lock, and for good when it never does.

concepts.title: Runtime directory
concepts.definition: The private directory under `/tmp` that holds what one worker run needs only while it runs, its generated configuration, credential copies, home, temporary and working directories, and that the host removes when the run ends.

contrasts.reason: the run directory is the worker run's trace node and is kept; the runtime directory holds what the worker needs only while it runs and is removed

concepts.title: Session boundary
concepts.definition: The Claude Code settings and write hook of its own that keep a task session's Edit and Write inside its task worktree and decision log, its one restriction, everything else of the session being left open.

concepts.title: Spec
concepts.definition: The documents in which a Module explains what it is for, how to use it, how it is designed and what it precisely promises.

concepts.title: Spec change
concepts.definition: The result of one specify run: the documents the worker changed, the documents the Operation created for it, the worker's account of the promises it changed, the Modules affected and the validation outcome.

concepts.title: Spec context
concepts.definition: The read-only documents the bound Modules' declarations select and the glossary entries of their terms: the Protocol's SpecContext of those Modules, which holds no external material and which a review-architecture task widens to every Module's documents and the whole glossary.

concepts.title: Spec gap
concepts.definition: A promise that the stated goal relies on and that the Spec of a bound Module does not state, reported with where it belongs instead of being inferred.

concepts.title: Standard worker sequence
concepts.definition: The fixed sequence by which a step of a Method Operation launches one worker: it admits the worker against the worker configuration and model map, computes and freezes the grant from the workspace's Specs, composes the task instructions, and hands the grant and its round validation to the worker harness, which prepares the settings and brief, launches the worker, audits it, resumes it with what the round validation reports and records the worker run.

concepts.title: Step agent
concepts.definition: The relay of a workflow step: a small Claude Code subagent that calls the `workflow_step` tool Workflows registers with the project MCP server once, waiting at most 100 seconds, while the step function asks again until the run has finished.

concepts.title: Step key
concepts.definition: The name of a workflow step within its workspace, made of the name the script gives it and, when a restart label or answers are passed, that label and a digest of those answers.

concepts.title: Structural check
concepts.definition: One decidable rule of the Spec Protocol or of Concorde's Spec conventions, named by a rule identity and carrying the strictness error or warning.

concepts.title: Task
concepts.definition: One unit of work of the main agent, made of a branch, a worktree checked out on it and bound as the workspace named after the task, and a folder in the primary worktree holding its task record, decision log and trace, which moves to the [history](#concept.history) when the task ends.

concepts.title: Task brief
concepts.definition: What the main agent records in a task's decision log before it starts the task's session: the developer's decisions the task carries out, the workflow and its mode when one applies, and what it leaves for the session to decide.

contrasts.reason: the task brief is the main agent's handoff of a task to a task session; a brief is the prompt an Operation generates for one worker

concepts.title: Task context
concepts.definition: The material produced for one task, namely its brief, constraints and admitted artifacts, which adds no Spec or code source.

concepts.title: Task record
concepts.definition: The JSON file `task.json` in a task's folder of the primary worktree that holds what the task commands need to act on it: its identity, goal, Modules, branch, worktree path, base commit, the main agent's session its task sessions report to now, stored state, the merge in progress and, once it ended, how it ended.

concepts.title: Task session
concepts.definition: A background Claude Code session to which the main agent delegates the work of one task, as it does for every task, working only inside that task's worktree until delivery and reporting to the main agent, to which it escalates together every decision the task needs that is not its own.

concepts.title: Task type
concepts.definition: One of the eight Protocol task types (understand, specify, implement, test, review-spec, review-code, code-to-spec, review-architecture), each the kind of one worker's job, that fixes the access level of every boundary set the job receives.

contrasts.reason: a task type is the kind of one worker's job in the Protocol's sense; a Task is the main agent's unit of work, a branch and worktree that has no task type

concepts.title: Test project
concepts.definition: A codebase cloned at a pinned revision into the end-to-end root, from SWE-bench's repositories unless `--any` admits another, with Concorde installed, initialized and a task open.

concepts.title: Trace
concepts.definition: The tree of [trace nodes](#concept.trace-node) below one root node, such as a task or an unbound run, nested as the work was: a task's sessions, merges and workspace, the workspace's workflow and runs, each run's checks and worker runs, each worker run's rounds.

concepts.title: Trace node
concepts.definition: The folder one level of work leaves, holding its `trace.json` record in one uniform shape (identity, kind, times, status, own usage, error link, metadata, artifacts, references and its producer's content) with its files and the folders of the nodes below it.

concepts.title: Typed value
concepts.definition: A versioned JSON record `{type_id, schema_version, data}` whose data is checked against the schema its owner registered for that type.

concepts.title: Unbound checkout
concepts.definition: The throwaway detached checkout of the HEAD of the worktree an unbound run started in, made as `.claude/worktrees/unbound-<run-id>` of the repository's primary worktree, in which the run's steps and workers work and which the runner removes before it writes the result.

concepts.title: Unbound run
concepts.definition: A run started in a worktree without a workspace binding, such as the primary worktree, which works in a throwaway detached checkout of that worktree's HEAD, records no workspace and may only read.

concepts.title: Verification declaration
concepts.definition: A statement in a test's own source that names the scenario identities the test verifies.

concepts.title: Worker
concepts.definition: One headless Claude Code or pi process that performs one bounded task of one task type under a frozen grant and reports only to the run that launched it through the worker harness.

concepts.title: Worker backend
concepts.definition: The agent program a worker runs on, Claude Code or pi: the one the worktree's worker configuration chooses for the worker or its Operation, otherwise pi; both enforce the same grant.

concepts.title: Worker configuration
concepts.definition: A worktree's Git-tracked `.concorde/workers.json`, required before any worker runs and the only source of a worker's model and reasoning level: the enabled models, each named by a project model name that depends on no installation and each with an optional level of its own, and a backend, a model and a reasoning level for every worker, for an Operation's workers and for one worker by its id, the most specific entry winning field by field, together with the limits of every worker launch and the runtime paths workers may read.

concepts.title: Worker id
concepts.definition: The stable name an Operation gives one worker it may launch, such as `spec_panel`'s `reviewer2` or `chair`, used alike in the worker configuration, the run record and the evidence.

concepts.title: Worker result
concepts.definition: The structured answer a worker ends with, validated against a fixed schema, reporting its status, a summary, its own error link when it could not finish, and the deletions it proposes.

concepts.title: Worker settings
concepts.definition: The Claude Code settings file the Harness generates from a grant, carrying the Bash sandbox, the deny rules and the write hook of one worker run.

concepts.title: Workflow
concepts.definition: A named procedure that orders the runs of one bound workspace and handles their results and decision points, written once and rendered as a Claude Code workflow.

concepts.title: Workflow mode
concepts.definition: Whether a workflow run is interactive, ending at the first decision point or the first step that did not end ok so that its decisions are settled above the task, through the main agent, before it goes on, or no-ask, keeping every decision its workers took and reporting it at the end.

concepts.title: Workflow record
concepts.definition: The `trace.json` of a workspace's workflow [trace node](#concept.trace-node), in which Workflows records the workflow's name, every step with its run and node, and every report.

concepts.title: Workflow result
concepts.definition: The envelope `concorde workflow report` assembles from the workflow record and the saved run results: status, steps, decisions, open questions, deviations, pending decision points, problems and the error chain.

concepts.title: Workflow script
concepts.definition: The JavaScript source of one workflow's procedure, contributed by the part that owns the procedure and rendered by the build, with Workflows' Claude Code step adapter, into a Claude Code workflow.

concepts.title: Workflow step
concepts.definition: One run of a workflow, of an Operation or an execution command, named by a step key and started and awaited through `concorde workflow step`, which returns the recorded run for a key it has seen before.

concepts.title: Workspace
concepts.definition: One worktree prepared for a bounded piece of work, with a name, a goal, the Modules it works on, the branch it works on and the commit it started from.

concepts.title: Workspace binding
concepts.definition: The file `.concorde/workspace.json` at a workspace's root that names it, its goal, Modules, branch and base commit, the workspace folder where its runs are traced and the `.concorde` whose `locks/` holds its locks, written by whoever prepares the workspace and only read by the parts that work in it.

concepts.title: Workspace lock
concepts.definition: The lock file `locks/workspaces/<workspace>.lock` of one workspace, held by the process running one of its runs from before that run's admission until after its result, or by whoever prepared the workspace while it merges or retires it, so that a workspace does one thing at a time.

concepts.title: Write audit
concepts.definition: The host's comparison, after each round and outside the worker, of the worktree's changes with the grant's `rw` list.

concepts.title: Write hook
concepts.definition: A small PreToolUse hook on Edit and Write that makes a worker's grant's `rw` list its exact write allowlist and explains every denial.
